judge_reasoning: All candidates broadly define Sobornost as a Russian Orthodox concept of conciliar/spiritual unity connected to the idea of “sobor” (council/assembly). Candidate 4 is the most prompt-faithful and grounded, giving a clear definition with a reasonable historical/thematic framing (Slavophiles/Church unity) and minimal detour. Candidate 1 and 3 are also correct in substance but are slightly less direct due to extra emphasis (later thinkers/Eucharistic or governance-oriented elaboration). Candidate 2 contains a good Sobornost explanation, but the substantial comparison to collectivism is an unrequested reframing that reduces focus.
